doc_drift.description: Documentation references deleted code or code without docs

duplicate_implementation.description: More than one file/service doing the same job

placeholder_code.description: TODO, FIXME, hardcoded data, stubs in production paths

dead_code.description: Unreferenced files, functions with no callers

missing_test.description: New logic without test coverage; disabled tests

config_drift.description: Hardcoded constants, naming divergence between config and code
config_drift.reason: Config changes can have unintended consequences

stale_adr.description: ADR marked Proposed long after code shipped; Accepted but implementation changed
stale_adr.reason: History preservation; status updates need verification

observability_gap.description: New service/route without status endpoint or logging
observability_gap.reason: Changes to running services require verification

resilience_gap.description: Missing error handling, retry logic, or fallbacks

router_bypass.description: Code calling Ollama or cloud provider directly instead of Model Router
router_bypass.reason: Router bypasses must be corrected by design review

route_policy_drift.description: Declared routes not used, used routes not declared, or undocumented routes

silent_fallback.description: Fallback that doesn't expose requested vs actual model or crosses trust boundaries
silent_fallback.reason: Silent data classification boundary changes require security review

model_catalogue_drift.description: Mismatch between configured, installed, preferred, and observed models

knowledge_health.description: Stale or incomplete knowledge base; missing context
knowledge_health.reason: Knowledge updates can affect model behavior

performance_gap.description: Detected performance regression or optimization opportunity
performance_gap.reason: Performance changes require validation against baselines

operational_failure.description: Service degradation, error rate, or operational issue detected

governance_violation.description: Code or deployment violates stated principles, ADRs, or policies

automation_opportunity.description: Opportunity to automate a manual process
automation_opportunity.reason: New automation requires design review and testing

maintenance.description: HQ Evolution generic bucket for a maintenance-class candidate with no precise legacy category (e.g. an evidence-derived candidate, not a model-analysed finding)
maintenance.reason: Generic bucket — deliberately more conservative than the precise legacy categories (doc_drift, dead_code) it's a fallback for; those keep their own auto-eligible rules unchanged

configuration.description: HQ Evolution generic bucket for a configuration-class candidate with no precise legacy category

reliability.description: HQ Evolution generic bucket for a reliability-class candidate with no precise legacy category

cost_optimisation.description: HQ Evolution: redundant LLM calls, duplicate synthesis, expensive-model-where-cheap-suffices, unused services, or other cost-reduction opportunity
cost_optimisation.reason: Auto-remediation of a cost opportunity is only ever permitted when it is bounded and reversible AND policy explicitly allows it for the specific action; none are pre-approved here. The PolicyEngine, not the model, remains the sole authority.

capability.description: HQ Evolution: a new tool/integration/architecture pattern that would give HQ a capability it does not have today
capability.reason: New capability requires a Mission — never bounded remediation, never auto-applied

product_improvement.description: HQ Evolution: a change to how an existing HQ surface behaves or prioritises (e.g. Brief prioritisation)
product_improvement.reason: Product-behaviour changes require a Mission / controlled build

architecture.description: HQ Evolution: replacing or restructuring a major subsystem
architecture.reason: Architecture-level change is Mission-only, always — the highest change class HQ Evolution can propose, never remediated directly

evolution.description: Bounds for the HQ Evolution overnight discovery cycle (scripts/self_improvement/evolution_orchestrator.py). Cheap filtering before expensive investigation: DISCOVER MANY -> RELEVANCE FILTER -> DEDUP -> SHORTLIST -> DEEP INVESTIGATION OF FEW. These bounds exist so overnight research cannot itself become an uncontrolled cost centre.
